title: Org-level burst pooling and reset propagation for linked tenants
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Context: Large customers frequently operate multiple Redwood tenants (projects) under a single paying organization. Today quotas and burst credits are tracked strictly per-tenant which can cause poor UX and surprising overages for orgs where one active tenant spikes while other tenants are idle. This ticket defines an org-level burst pooling model and deterministic reset propagation so organization owners get predictable behavior and operators can avoid ad hoc billing credits.

Goals: 
- Allow organizations to opt into a pooled-burst bucket that aggregates unused short-term burst capacity from linked tenants.
- Ensure deterministic, auditable monthly/daily reset semantics across both pooled and per-tenant buckets.
- Preserve reserved-capacity guarantees for contracts that purchased dedicated pools unless the org opts into an explicit pooling override.
- Provide clear admin controls: enable/disable pooling, set per-tenant floor, and emergency throttles.

Non-goals: 
- Replacing per-tenant billing or metering: invoicing remains per-tenant/org as currently implemented.
- Real-time cross-region rebalancing of dedicated GPUs (out of scope).

Design overview: 
1) Data model: add an OrgBurstBucket entity keyed by organization_id with fields: current_tokens, window_start, pooled_source_snapshot (hash). Implemented as ledger entries in the existing quota ledger to preserve auditability.
2) Allocation policy: weight-based pooling where each linked tenant contributes its instantaneous unused burst capacity up to a configurable cap (default: 30% of tenant burst). Tenant weights default to equal but admin can specify weights. When an API request arrives for a tenant, evaluation order: tenant burst -> org pool -> reserved capacity (if applicable) -> fallback.
3) Reset semantics: daily rolling windows are calculated per-tenant; org pool has independent daily/monthly checkpoints derived from contributor snapshots. Monthly resets occur on the org billing anchor (customer-configurable timezone); propagation guarantees: org pool snapshot is applied deterministically before per-tenant resets to avoid double-counting.
4) Fairness & safeguards: tenants retain a configurable minimum floor (default 10% of their nominal monthly quota) to avoid starvation by aggressive org consumers. Implement soft-guard throttling that begins to deprioritize traffic when an org's pooled spend exceeds a threshold (e.g., 80% of pooled capacity) and hard caps that return 429 when beyond absolute limits.
5) Reserved capacity interactions: tenants with reserved pools continue to draw from their reserved allocation first; only overflow is eligible for contribution to the org pool (admin toggle). Reserved pool customers can opt out of contributing.
6) Telemetry & audit: emit events for pool contributions, pool draws, and reset reconciliation with originating tenant IDs, ledger offsets, and causation IDs. Add dashboards: org-pool-utilization, tenant-contribution-latency, pooled-overage-incidents.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Can enable org pooling via API and Console for an org; pool behaves deterministically in integration tests.
- Pool contribution and draw events are visible in ledger and Console with correct attribution.
- Monthly reset order produces identical final balances when run repeatedly (idempotence).
- Admin floor prevents tenant-level starvation in synthetic stress tests.
- Migration and rollback runbooks exist and have been exercised in staging.

Trade-offs considered: 
- Strong consistency vs eventual ledger convergence: chosen approach relies on ledger-backed snapshots and a short-lived optimistic lock to avoid global serial bottlenecks. This favors correctness and auditability at the cost of a small window of increased latency on pool commit steps.
- Complexity of weight configuration vs simplicity: default equal weights to reduce customer configuration surface while allowing per-tenant weights for orgs that need fine control.

Rollout plan: 
- Phase 1 (canary): Feature-flagged rollout to 5 low-risk orgs in staging; monitor pool accounting, 429 rates, and reconciliation diffs.
- Phase 2 (beta): Open to selected production orgs via opt-in; expose admin toggles in Console, add an activity log export.
- Phase 3 (GA): Default opt-out for all orgs; add migration job to compute initial org-pool snapshots for orgs that opt in post-GA.

Migration & rollback: 
- One-time migration job computes pool snapshots using last 30 days of usage; job writes to ledger with tombstone markers for audit.
- Rollback: mark feature flag off and replay ledger tombstones to restore per-tenant-only accounting; run reconciliation to validate balances.

Open questions: 
- Should org pools be allowed to borrow across monthly boundaries (short-term credit)? (product/finance)
- Billing: how should pooled usage appear on invoices (line item vs rollup)? (billing/finance)
- TTL for stale pool contributors when tenants are deleted.

Notes: This ticket interacts with rate limiting path, reserved capacity mechanism, and existing quota reset code. We will coordinate with product for UX copy and with finance for invoice representation.
